prompt: You are given $A = 40^\circ$, $a = 8$ and $b = 10$. How many triangles fit this description?
hint: This is the SSA arrangement — the famous ambiguous case.

hints.text: This is the SSA arrangement — the famous ambiguous case.
Compute the height $h = b\sin A = 10\sin 40^\circ \approx 6.43$ and compare it with $a$ and $b$.
Since $6.43 < 8 < 10$, the side $a$ can swing to meet the base in two different places: two triangles.

explanation: With two sides and a non-included angle (SSA), the given side can sometimes reach the base in two ways.
The critical height is $h = b\sin A = 10\sin 40^\circ \approx 6.43$.
Because $h < a < b$, that is $6.43 < 8 < 10$, side $a$ is long enough to reach but short enough to reach twice.
So there are two possible triangles, one with an acute angle $B$ and one with an obtuse angle $B$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the swinging side
steps: Draw angle $A$ and lay side $b = 10$ along one arm.
Now put a compass at the far end of $b$ and swing an arc of radius $a = 8$ toward the other arm.
If the arc falls short there is no triangle; if it just touches there is one; if it cuts across there are two. Here it cuts across.
